content: 1. Iron Field MS, Mithra P, and Pena-Rosas JP conducted a study on the fortification of wheat flour with iron and other micronutrients. Their research aimed to evaluate its effectiveness in reducing anemia and improving iron status in populations. This study was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2021 (Issue 1, Article CD011302). 2. Sadighi J, Nedjat S, and Rostami R performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the global impact of iron-fortified flour on the iron status of populations. Their findings were published in Public Health Nutrition in 2019 (Volume 22, Pages 3465–3484, DOI: 10.1017/S1368980019002179). 3. Keats E, Neufeld L, Garrett G, Mbuya M, and Bhutta Z reviewed evidence from large-scale fortification programs in lowand middle-income countries. Their systematic review and meta-analysis demonstrated improved micronutrient status and health outcomes. This study was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2019 (Volume 109, Pages 1696–1708, DOI: 10.1093/ajcn/nqz023). 4. Pachon H, Spohrer R, Mei Z, and Serdula MK conducted a systematic review to evaluate the effectiveness of flour fortification programs on iron status and anemia. Their findings were published in Nutrition Reviews in 2015 (Volume 73, Pages 780–795, DOI: 10.1093/nutrit/nuv037). 5. Athe R, Rao MVV, and Nair KM analyzed the impact of iron-fortified foods on hemoglobin concentration in children under 10 years of age. Their systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials were published in Public Health Nutrition in 2014 (Volume 17, Pages 579–586, DOI: 10.1017/S1368980013000062). 6. Das J, Salam R, Kumar R, and Bhutta Z conducted a systematic review on the impact of micronutrient fortification of food on the health of women and children. Their findings were published in Systematic Reviews in 2013 (Volume 2, Article 67, DOI: 10.1186/2046-4053-2-67). 7. Gera T, Sachdev HS, and Boy E reviewed randomized controlled trials to assess the effects of iron-fortified foods on hematologic and biological outcomes. Their systematic review was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2012 (Volume 96, Pages 309–324, DOI: 10.031500). 8. Centeno Tablante E, Pachon H, Guetterman HM, and Finkelstein JL reviewed the fortification of wheat and maize flour with folic acid and its impact on population health outcomes. Their study was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2019 (Issue 7, Article CD012150). 9. Shah D, Sachdev HS, Gera T, De-Regil LM, and Pena-Rosas JP conducted a systematic review on the fortification of staple foods with zinc to improve zinc status and other health outcomes in the general population. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2016 (Issue 6, Article CD010697). 10. Tsang B, Holsted E, McDonald C, Brown K, Black R, Mbuya M, and colleagues reviewed the effects of zinc-fortified foods, either alone or co-fortified with multiple micronutrients, on health and functional outcomes. Their systematic review and meta-analysis were published in Advances in Nutrition in 2021 (Volume 12, Issue 5, Pages 1821–1837, DOI: 10.1093/advances/nmab065). An erratum was later published in the same journal (Volume 12, Issue 5, Pages 2040–2044). 11. Hombali AS, Solon JA, Venkatesh BT, Nair NS, and Pena-Rosas JP reviewed the fortification of staple foods with vitamin A to address vitamin A deficiency. Their findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2019 (Issue 5, Article CD010068).
